subproblems.title: Tangent planes exist a.e., are measurable, and density = multiplicity a.e. (Simon Ch. 3, 1.6-1.9)
subproblems.statement: Let n >= 1, l >= 0, U an open subset of R^(n+l), and V a rectifiable n-varifold in U in the sense of the contract (carrier M contained in U, H^n-null-measurable and countably n-rectifiable; multiplicity theta positive on M, H^n-a.e.-measurable on M and H^n-integrable on M cap K for each compact K contained in U), mu := V.weight = theta H^n restricted to M. Then: (i) x -> V.tangentProj x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable; (ii) for mu-a.e. x there is an n-dimensional subspace P with V.tangentProj x = P.starProjection (the approximate tangent space of M with respect to theta, Simon Ch. 3, 1.7, exists at mu-a.e. x); (iii) for mu-a.e. x, V.HasDensity x (V.mult x), i.e. mu(B_r(x))/(omega_n r^n) -> theta(x) as r -> 0+.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U, AEStronglyMeasurable V.tangentProj V.weight ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, ∃ P : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), Module.finrank ℝ P = n ∧ V.tangentProj x = P.starProjection) ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, V.HasDensity x (V.mult x))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused verbatim: this is the independently reviewed proof frozen for DAG node root.allard_regularity-a1.tangent_ae-a1 (status accepted, candidate 9f4dca6), whose Lean declaration Submission.allard52_tangent_ae has exactly this frozen type. In the selected node, conclusions (i) and (ii) are the two facts that step 0 of the supplied proof takes from tangent_ae; (iii) is part of the accepted type but is not used there.

Source: Simon, Ch. 3, Def. 1.4, 1.7, Lemma 1.2, Rem. 1.3, Thm. 1.6 ('=>'), Rem. 1.8(1),(2), Thm. 1.9 (the fact (F1) of the parent proof), with the measurability step made explicit.

Notation. M := V.carrier (a subset of U), theta := V.mult, mu := V.weight = theta H^n restricted to M (theta := 0 off M), p_x := V.tangentProj x, eta_{x,r}(w) := (w - x)/r, B_r(x) the closed ball, B^o_r(x) the open ball, omega_n := unitBallVolume n; for an n-dimensional subspace P, p_P := P.starProjection. Hypotheses: U open; M is H^n-null-measurable and countably n-rectifiable; theta > 0 on M, theta is H^n-a.e.-measurable on M, and theta is H^n-integrable on M cap K for every compact K contained in U.

1. Two reductions.
 (a) mu(R^(n+l) minus M) = 0, and a set N contained in M is mu-null iff it is H^n-null: if H^n(N) = 0 then mu(N) = 0; conversely, if mu(N) = 0 take an H^n-measurable N' containing N with mu(N' cap M) = 0 (measurable hull); then integral_{N' cap M} theta dH^n = 0 with theta > 0 on M forces H^n(N' cap M) = 0. Hence (ii) and (iii) follow once they are proved at H^n-a.e. x in M, and (i) follows once p is shown to be a mu-a.e. limit of Borel maps.
 (b) [Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.7 = SimonGMT Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt, the predicate used to define tangentProj] An n-dimensional subspace P is an approximate tangent space of M w.r.t. theta at x if lim_{r -> 0+} integral_{eta_{x,r}(M)} f(z) theta(x + r z) dH^n(z) = theta(x) integral_P f dH^n for every f in C_c(R^(n+l)). Since H^n(x + r E) = r^n H^n(E), for x in U and r so small that x + r spt f is a compact subset of U,
 (*) integral_{eta_{x,r}(M)} f(z) theta(x + r z) dH^n(z) = r^-n integral_M f((w - x)/r) theta(w) dH^n(w) = r^-n integral f((w - x)/r) dmu(w),
 and this integral is finite because theta is H^n-integrable on M cap K for compact K in U. If x in M then theta(x) > 0, so such a P is unique (SimonGMT HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), and by the definition of tangentProj, p_x = p_P whenever such a P exists; then dim P = n.

2. Localization. Let U_k := {x : |x| < k and B_{1/k}(x) is contained in U} (closed balls; this avoids distances to a possibly empty complement). U_k is open (if B_{1/k}(x) is contained in U then, by compactness, so is B_{1/k + eps}(x) for some eps > 0), its closure is a compact subset of U (if x_m -> x with B_{1/k}(x_m) in U then B^o_{1/k}(x) is contained in U, so x in U, and the closure is bounded), and U = union_k U_k (U is open). Put M_k := M cap U_k: it is H^n-measurable, countably n-rectifiable (a subset of M) and integral_{M_k cap K} theta dH^n < infinity for every compact K in R^(n+l). If x in M_k, spt f is contained in B_rho'(0) and r rho' is so small that B_{r rho'}(x) is contained in U_k (possible since U_k is open), then f((w - x)/r) != 0 implies w in U_k, so the integrals (*) for (M, theta) and for (M_k, theta) coincide; hence the approximate tangent spaces of (M, theta) and (M_k, theta) at x coincide (existence and value), and mu(B_r(x)) = (theta H^n restricted to M_k)(B_r(x)) for small r. As M = union_k M_k, it suffices to prove (ii) and (iii) at H^n-a.e. point of each M_k for the pair (M_k, theta), which satisfies the global hypotheses of Simon Ch. 3, 1.7-1.9. In steps 3 and 4 we therefore assume integral_{M cap K} theta dH^n < infinity for every compact K, so that mu is a Radon measure on R^(n+l).

3. Existence of T_x(M, theta) for H^n-a.e. x in M (Simon Ch. 3, Thm. 1.9).
 (a) [Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 and Rem. 1.3] Since M is countably n-rectifiable there are an H^n-null set N_0 and embedded n-dimensional C^1 submanifolds N_1, N_2, ... of R^(n+l) with M contained in union_{j >= 0} N_j. (Proof of Lemma 1.2: M is contained in N'_0 union union_i F_i(R^n) with H^n(N'_0) = 0 and F_i Lipschitz; by the C^1 approximation theorem (Ch. 2, 1.5; its Whitney-extension core is SimonGMT Chapter02.exists_contDiff_one_extension_of_whitney) each F_i coincides, outside sets of arbitrarily small L^n-measure, with C^1 maps G_ij; by the area formula G_ij({J G_ij = 0}) is H^n-null, and each point of {J G_ij != 0} has a neighbourhood whose G_ij-image is an embedded n-dimensional C^1 submanifold (inverse function theorem); countably many such neighbourhoods suffice.) The cover can be disjointified into H^n-measurable pieces (SimonGMT Chapter03.simon_remark_1_3).
 (b) [Ch. 3, Rem. 1.8(1)] H^n restricted to M is sigma-finite (H^n(M cap K cap {theta > 1/j}) <= j integral_{M cap K} theta). By Lusin's theorem there are compact sets K_1, K_2, ... contained in M, increasing, with H^n(M minus union_i K_i) = 0 and theta restricted to K_i continuous; theta has a positive minimum c_i on K_i, so H^n(K_i) <= c_i^-1 integral_{K_i} theta < infinity. By the upper density theorem (Ch. 1, 3.6; SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6) applied to the Radon measure mu restricted to (M minus K_i), there is an H^n-null set E_i such that r^-n mu(B_r(x) minus K_i) -> 0 as r -> 0 for every x in K_i minus E_i.
 (c) [Ch. 3, Thm. 1.6 '=>' for K_i] Fix i and put K_ij := K_i cap N_j minus union_{j' < j} N_j' (so H^n(K_i0) = 0). Fix j >= 1. N_j is covered by countably many open sets W in which N_j cap W is a C^1 graph of finite H^n-measure. By the upper density theorem for the finite measures H^n restricted to (K_i minus K_ij) and H^n restricted to ((N_j cap W) minus K_ij), for H^n-a.e. x in K_ij cap W both measures have zero n-dimensional density at x. Since N_j is C^1 at x, lim_{r -> 0} integral_{eta_{x,r}(N_j)} f dH^n = integral_{T_x N_j} f dH^n for f in C_c. Writing integral_{eta_{x,r}(K_i)} f = integral_{eta_{x,r}(N_j)} f - integral_{eta_{x,r}(N_j minus K_ij)} f + integral_{eta_{x,r}(K_i minus K_ij)} f and bounding the last two terms (for spt f in B_rho'(0)) by sup|f| r^-n H^n(B_{rho' r}(x) cap (N_j minus K_ij)) and sup|f| r^-n H^n(B_{rho' r}(x) cap (K_i minus K_ij)), which tend to 0, we get lim integral_{eta_{x,r}(K_i)} f dH^n = integral_{T_x N_j} f dH^n: the unweighted approximate tangent space T_x K_i (Def. 1.4) exists and equals T_x N_j. Hence T_x K_i exists for H^n-a.e. x in K_i.
 (d) [Ch. 3, Rem. 1.8(1)] Let x in K_i minus E_i be a point at which P := T_x K_i exists, and let f in C_c with spt f in B_rho'(0). By (*), integral_{eta_{x,r}(M)} f(z) theta(x + r z) dH^n(z) = r^-n integral_{K_i} f((w - x)/r) theta(w) dH^n(w) + r^-n integral_{M minus K_i} f((w - x)/r) dmu(w). The second term is at most sup|f| r^-n mu(B_{rho' r}(x) minus K_i) -> 0 by (b). In the first term |theta(w) - theta(x)| <= eps_r -> 0 uniformly for w in K_i cap B_{rho' r}(x) (continuity of theta on K_i), and r^-n H^n(K_i cap B_{rho' r}(x)) stays bounded (it converges to omega_n rho'^n by (c) applied to test functions squeezing the indicator of B_rho'(0)); hence the first term equals theta(x) integral_{eta_{x,r}(K_i)} f dH^n + o(1) -> theta(x) integral_P f dH^n. So P is the approximate tangent space of M w.r.t. theta at x.
 Since H^n(M minus union_i K_i) = 0 and every E_i is H^n-null, T_x(M, theta) exists for H^n-a.e. x in M. By 1(a),(b) this proves (ii): for mu-a.e. x there is an n-dimensional P with V.tangentProj x = P.starProjection.

4. Density (iii) (Ch. 3, Rem. 1.8(2)). Let x in M be such that P := T_x(M, theta) exists. For eps in (0,1) choose continuous compactly supported g_eps, h_eps : R^(n+l) -> [0,1] with g_eps = 1 on B_1(0), g_eps = 0 outside B_{1+eps}(0), h_eps = 1 on B_{1-eps}(0) and h_eps = 0 outside B^o_1(0). By (*), r^-n integral h_eps((w - x)/r) dmu <= r^-n mu(B_r(x)) <= r^-n integral g_eps((w - x)/r) dmu, and as r -> 0 the outer terms converge to theta(x) integral_P h_eps dH^n >= theta(x) omega_n (1 - eps)^n and to theta(x) integral_P g_eps dH^n <= theta(x) omega_n (1 + eps)^n (H^n on P is n-dimensional Lebesgue measure, H^n(P cap B_t(0)) = omega_n t^n). Letting eps -> 0, mu(B_r(x))/(omega_n r^n) -> theta(x) in (0, infinity); in extended reals, mu(B_r(x)) / ofReal(omega_n r^n) -> ofReal(theta(x)) as r -> 0+, i.e. V.HasDensity x (V.mult x). By step 3 and 1(a) this holds for mu-a.e. x.

5. Measurability (i). Let phi(t) := max{0, 1 - t} (t >= 0), c_0 := integral_{R^n} phi(|t|) dt > 0 and c_1 := (1/n) integral_{R^n} phi(|t|) |t|^2 dt > 0. For an n-dimensional subspace P with orthonormal basis tau_1, ..., tau_n, the isometric parametrization t -> sum_k t_k tau_k gives integral_P phi(|z|) dH^n(z) = c_0 and integral_P phi(|z|) z (x) z dH^n(z) = sum_{k,k'} (integral phi(|t|) t_k t_k' dt) tau_k (x) tau_k' = c_1 p_P (mixed moments vanish by the symmetry t_k -> -t_k, and integral phi(|t|) t_k^2 dt = c_1 for each k). For k >= 1 let W_k := {x : B_{2/k}(x) is contained in U} (open, as in step 2; U = union_k W_k) and for x in W_k set
 a_k(x) := k^n integral phi(k |w - x|) dmu(w), b_k(x) := k^(n+2) integral phi(k |w - x|) (w - x) (x) (w - x) dmu(w)
 (b_k(x) is a linear operator on R^(n+l)). The integrands are bounded, continuous in x and supported in B_{1/k}(x); for x within 1/k of a point x_0 in W_k these balls lie in the compact set B_{2/k}(x_0), contained in U, on which mu is finite, so a_k, b_k are continuous on W_k by dominated convergence. Define h_k(x) := (c_0/c_1) b_k(x)/a_k(x) if x in W_k and a_k(x) > 0, and h_k(x) := 0 otherwise; each h_k is Borel. If x in M and P = T_x(M, theta) exists, then x in W_k for large k and, by (*) with r = 1/k and the compactly supported continuous test functions z -> phi(|z|) and z -> phi(|z|) z_i z_j, a_k(x) -> theta(x) c_0 > 0 and b_k(x) -> theta(x) c_1 p_P; hence h_k(x) -> p_P = p_x by 1(b). By step 3 this convergence holds for mu-a.e. x. So p is the mu-a.e. limit of Borel, hence strongly measurable, maps into the finite-dimensional space of operators on R^(n+l), and is therefore mu-a.e. strongly measurable (Mathlib aestronglyMeasurable_of_tendsto_ae). This proves (i), and with steps 3 and 4 the theorem.
proof_key_steps: Reduce to H^n-a.e. statements on M and localize to pieces M_k on which theta is globally integrable
Cover M by C^1 submanifolds (Ch. 3, 1.2/1.3) and split by Lusin into compact pieces K_i with continuous theta
Upper density theorem gives T_x K_i = T_x N_j a.e. (Thm 1.6) and then the weighted tangent space T_x(M, theta) (Rem 1.8(1))
Squeezing test functions gives density = theta (Rem 1.8(2))
Second-moment quotients h_k are Borel and converge a.e. to p_x, so tangentProj is a.e. strongly measurable

subproblems.title: Tilt bounded by L2 height and sup-height times L1 mean curvature (Lemma A)
subproblems.statement: Let n >= 1, l, U open, V with generalized mean curvature H in U, x |-> p_x mu-a.e. strongly measurable and mu-a.e. the orthogonal projection onto an n-dimensional subspace. If z in R^{n+l}, r > 0 with B_r(z) in U, h >= 0, T is an n-dimensional subspace and infDist(x - z, T) <= h for every x in spt V cap B_r(z), then int_{B_{r/2}(z)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu <= 144 r^{-2} int_{B_r(z)} dist(x - z, T)^2 dmu + 4 h int_{B_r(z)} |H| dmu. (Here V is a contract rectifiable n-varifold in U, i.e. RectifiableVarifold n l U, mu = V.weight, p_x = V.tangentProj x, p_T = T.starProjection, spt V = V.support, |.| is the Hilbert-Schmidt norm (|A|^2 = hsNormSq A), balls are closed and all integrals are Bochner integrals with respect to mu.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ n ℓ : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ), V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H → AEStronglyMeasurable V.tangentProj V.weight → (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, ∃ P : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), Module.finrank ℝ P = n ∧ V.tangentProj x = P.starProjection) → ∀ (z : Amb n ℓ) (r h : ℝ), 0 < r → closedBall z r ⊆ U → 0 ≤ h → ∀ T : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), Module.finrank ℝ T = n → (∀ x ∈ V.support ∩ closedBall z r, infDist (x - z) (T : Set (Amb n ℓ)) ≤ h) → ∫ x in closedBall z (r / 2), hsNormSq (V.tangentProj x - T.starProjection) ∂V.weight ≤ 144 * (r ^ 2)⁻¹ * ∫ x in closedBall z r, infDist (x - z) (T : Set (Amb n ℓ)) ^ 2 ∂V.weight + 4 * h * ∫ x in closedBall z r, ‖H x‖ ∂V.weight
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Lemma A of the selected node's supplied proof (the L^1 form of the computation proving Simon Ch. 5, Lemma 2.1, p. 107), steps 0-6, specialized so that the two tangent-plane facts which the supplied proof takes from tangent_ae are the hypotheses (Hmeas) and (Hproj) of this child. This is the statement of the accepted DAG node root.tilt_excess_decay-a1.lemma_a_tilt_height-a1, whose frozen Lean type is reused verbatim.

Setting and notation. n >= 1, l >= 0, m := n + l, U an open subset of R^m, V a contract RectifiableVarifold n l U with carrier M (contained in U) and multiplicity theta (theta > 0 on M, theta H^n-integrable on M cap K for every compact K contained in U), mu := V.weight = (H^n restricted to M) with density ofReal(theta), spt V := V.support = U cap spt mu, p_x := V.tangentProj x. H : R^m -> R^m satisfies V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H, i.e. (G1) H is locally mu-integrable on U, and (G2) integral div_M X dmu = - integral <X, H> dmu for every C^1 map X : R^m -> R^m with compact support and tsupport X contained in U, where div_M X(x) = trace(DX(x) o p_x). Further hypotheses: (Hmeas) x -> p_x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable; (Hproj) for mu-a.e. x there is an n-dimensional subspace P with p_x = P.starProjection; z in R^m, r > 0 with B_r(z) contained in U (closed ball), h >= 0; T an n-dimensional subspace; (Hh) infDist(x - z, T) <= h for every x in spt V cap B_r(z). Put p_T := T.starProjection, Q := I - p_T (the orthogonal projection onto the orthogonal complement of T) and x' := Q(x - z). For a linear map A of R^m: |A|^2 := hsNormSq A = sum_i |A e_i|^2 (e_i the standard basis), |A| := hsNorm A, ||A|| the operator norm. B^o_s(z) is the open ball. All integrals are Bochner integrals with respect to mu.

Claim. integral_{B_{r/2}(z)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu <= 144 (r^2)^(-1) integral_{B_r(z)} infDist(x - z, T)^2 dmu + 4 h integral_{B_r(z)} |H| dmu.

0. Preliminaries.
 (a) mu(B_r(z)) < infinity. B_r(z) is compact and contained in U, so the contract field integrableOn_mult gives integral_{M cap B_r(z)} theta dH^n < infinity; by the definition of mu (a density on H^n restricted to M), mu(B_r(z)) = integral_{M cap B_r(z)} ofReal(theta) dH^n < infinity.
 (b) H is mu-integrable on B_r(z), since by (G1) a function locally integrable on U is integrable on every compact subset of U.
 (c) mu-a.e. x lies in spt V. Indeed mu(R^m minus spt mu) = 0 (R^m is second countable), and mu(R^m minus U) <= mu(R^m minus M) = 0 because mu is absolutely continuous with respect to H^n restricted to M and M is contained in U.
 (d) Linear algebra. Let P be an n-dimensional subspace and p_P := P.starProjection. Both p_P and p_T are self-adjoint idempotents of trace n (the trace of an orthogonal projection is its rank).
  (OP) ||A|| <= |A| for every linear A: for v = sum_i v_i e_i, |A v| = |sum_i v_i A e_i| <= sum_i |v_i| |A e_i| <= (sum_i v_i^2)^(1/2) (sum_i |A e_i|^2)^(1/2) = |v| |A| (triangle and Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities).
  (DI) |Q v| = infDist(v, T) for every v: p_T v lies in T, and for every t in T, |v - t|^2 = |v - p_T v|^2 + |p_T v - t|^2 >= |v - p_T v|^2 because v - p_T v is orthogonal to T; hence |Q v| = |v - p_T v| = infDist(v, T). In particular |x'| = infDist(x - z, T) <= |x - z| (as 0 lies in T).
  (TR) trace(Q o p_P) = (1/2)|p_P - p_T|^2. With A := p_P - p_T (self-adjoint), |A|^2 = sum_i <A e_i, A e_i> = sum_i <A^2 e_i, e_i> = trace(A^2) = trace(p_P) + trace(p_T) - trace(p_P p_T) - trace(p_T p_P) = 2n - 2 trace(p_T p_P), using p_P^2 = p_P, p_T^2 = p_T and trace(p_P p_T) = trace(p_T p_P); and trace(Q p_P) = trace(p_P) - trace(p_T p_P) = n - trace(p_T p_P).
  (BD) |p_P - p_T|^2 <= (|p_P| + |p_T|)^2 = 4n, because |p_P|^2 = sum_i <p_P e_i, e_i> = trace(p_P) = n (likewise |p_T|^2 = n) and |.| is a norm (the Euclidean norm of the matrix entries); also ||p_P - p_T|| <= ||p_P|| + ||p_T|| <= 2.
  By (Hproj), (BD) gives |p_x - p_T|^2 <= 4n and ||p_x - p_T|| <= 2 for mu-a.e. x.

1. Cutoff. Let S : R -> [0, 1] be C^infinity with S = 0 on (-infinity, 0] and S = 1 on [1, infinity) (for instance Mathlib's smoothTransition). Put beta(t) := S(12(t - 1/2)) S(12(1 - t)). Then beta is C^infinity, 0 <= beta <= 1, beta = 0 outside (1/2, 1) and beta = 1 on [7/12, 11/12], so c := integral_R beta lies in [1/3, 1/2]. Define phi(t) := 1 - c^(-1) integral_{-infinity}^t beta. Then phi is C^infinity with phi' = -beta/c, hence -3 <= phi' <= 0; phi = 1 on (-infinity, 1/2], phi = 0 on [1, infinity), 0 <= phi <= 1, and phi is 3-Lipschitz by the mean value theorem. Put zeta(x) := phi(|x - z|/r). Then:
 - 0 <= zeta <= 1, zeta = 1 on B_{r/2}(z), and zeta(x) = 0 whenever |x - z| >= r;
 - zeta is C^infinity: zeta = 1 on the open ball B^o_{r/2}(z) (there |x - z|/r < 1/2), and near every x != z the map y -> |y - z| is C^infinity (the Euclidean norm is smooth away from 0), so zeta is C^infinity near x by composition; these open sets cover R^m;
 - zeta is (3/r)-Lipschitz, since |zeta(x) - zeta(y)| <= 3 ||x - z| - |y - z|| / r <= (3/r)|x - y|; hence ||D zeta(x)|| <= 3/r for every x;
 - D zeta(x) = 0 whenever |x - z| > r, because zeta vanishes on that open set.

2. Test field. X(x) := zeta(x)^2 x' = zeta(x)^2 Q(x - z). X is C^infinity (the C^infinity scalar zeta^2 times an affine map). If X(x) != 0 then zeta(x) != 0, so |x - z| < r; hence tsupport X is contained in B_r(z), which is contained in U, and X has compact support. By (G2), integral div_M X dmu = - integral <X, H> dmu; both integrands are integrable by step 4.

3. Divergence. By the product rule, DX(x) v = zeta(x)^2 Q v + 2 zeta(x) (D zeta(x) v) x' for all x and v. Fix x with p_x = p_P for an n-dimensional subspace P (mu-a.e. x, by (Hproj)). Then
 div_M X(x) = trace(DX(x) o p_P) = zeta(x)^2 trace(Q o p_P) + 2 zeta(x) trace(v -> (D zeta(x)(p_P v)) x') = zeta(x)^2 trace(Q o p_P) + 2 zeta(x) D zeta(x)(p_P x'),
 since the trace of a rank-one map v -> lambda(v) w equals lambda(w). As p_T x' = p_T Q(x - z) = 0, we have p_P x' = (p_P - p_T) x'. Writing s(x) := (1/2)|p_x - p_T|^2 >= 0 and using (TR):
 (D) div_M X(x) = zeta(x)^2 s(x) + 2 zeta(x) D zeta(x)((p_x - p_T) x') for mu-a.e. x.

4. Measurability and integrability. By (Hmeas), x -> p_x - p_T is mu-a.e. strongly measurable; composing with the continuous maps A -> |A|^2 and A -> ||A||, applying the continuous bilinear evaluation (A, x) -> D zeta(x)(A Q(x - z)), and multiplying by continuous functions of x preserves mu-a.e. strong measurability. Hence zeta^2 s, the cross term c(x) := 2 zeta(x) D zeta(x)((p_x - p_T) x') and ||D zeta||^2 |x'|^2 are mu-a.e. strongly measurable; they vanish when |x - z| > r (zeta = 0 and D zeta = 0 there), and mu-a.e. on B_r(z) they satisfy zeta^2 s <= 2n, |c| <= 2 (3/r)(2)(r) = 12 and ||D zeta||^2 |x'|^2 <= 9 (using |x'| <= |x - z| <= r and ||p_x - p_T|| <= 2). The functions <X, H> and zeta^2 |x'| |H| are products of H (respectively |H|), which is integrable on B_r(z) by 0(b), with continuous functions bounded by r that vanish outside B_r(z); so |<X, H>| <= zeta^2 |x'| |H| <= r |H| 1_{B_r(z)}. Since mu(B_r(z)) < infinity by 0(a), all of these functions are mu-integrable, and by (D) div_M X agrees mu-a.e. with the integrable function zeta^2 s + c. Likewise x -> |p_x - p_T|^2 is integrable on B_{r/2}(z) (bounded by 4n a.e. on a set of finite measure), and infDist(x - z, T)^2 (continuous, at most r^2 on B_r(z)) and |H| are integrable on B_r(z); so every integral in the claim is the integral of an integrable function.

5. Identity and absorption. Integrating (D) and using step 2:
 (I) integral zeta^2 s dmu = - integral c dmu - integral zeta^2 <x', H> dmu.
 Pointwise mu-a.e., by (OP) and |p_x - p_T| = sqrt(2 s):
 |c| <= 2 zeta ||D zeta|| ||p_x - p_T|| |x'| <= 2 zeta ||D zeta|| |p_x - p_T| |x'| = 2 (zeta sqrt(s)/sqrt(2)) (2 ||D zeta|| |x'|) <= (1/2) zeta^2 s + 4 ||D zeta||^2 |x'|^2 (by 2ab <= a^2 + b^2),
 and - zeta^2 <x', H> <= zeta^2 |x'| |H|. Integrating these bounds in (I) gives
 integral zeta^2 s <= (1/2) integral zeta^2 s + 4 integral ||D zeta||^2 |x'|^2 + integral zeta^2 |x'| |H|.
 Since integral zeta^2 s is a finite real number, subtracting (1/2) integral zeta^2 s and doubling yields
 (A) integral zeta^2 s dmu <= 8 integral ||D zeta||^2 |x'|^2 dmu + 2 integral zeta^2 |x'| |H| dmu.

6. Conclusion.
 - Since zeta = 1 on B_{r/2}(z) and zeta^2 s >= 0 is integrable: (1/2) integral_{B_{r/2}(z)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu = integral_{B_{r/2}(z)} zeta^2 s dmu <= integral zeta^2 s dmu.
 - For every x, ||D zeta(x)||^2 |x'|^2 <= 9 r^(-2) 1_{B_r(z)}(x) infDist(x - z, T)^2: if |x - z| > r then D zeta(x) = 0; otherwise ||D zeta(x)|| <= 3/r and |x'| = infDist(x - z, T) by (DI). Hence 8 integral ||D zeta||^2 |x'|^2 dmu <= 72 r^(-2) integral_{B_r(z)} infDist(x - z, T)^2 dmu.
 - For mu-a.e. x: if x is not in B_r(z) then zeta(x) = 0; if x is in B_r(z) then x lies in spt V by 0(c), so |x'| = infDist(x - z, T) <= h by (DI) and (Hh), while zeta^2 <= 1. Thus zeta^2 |x'| |H| <= h |H| 1_{B_r(z)} mu-a.e., and 2 integral zeta^2 |x'| |H| dmu <= 2 h integral_{B_r(z)} |H| dmu.
 Inserting the three bullets into (A): (1/2) integral_{B_{r/2}(z)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu <= 72 r^(-2) integral_{B_r(z)} infDist(x - z, T)^2 dmu + 2 h integral_{B_r(z)} |H| dmu. Multiplying by 2 gives integral_{B_{r/2}(z)} hsNormSq(V.tangentProj x - T.starProjection) dmu <= 144 (r^2)^(-1) integral_{B_r(z)} infDist(x - z, T)^2 dmu + 4 h integral_{B_r(z)} ||H x|| dmu, which is the claim.
proof_key_steps: Preliminaries: mu(B_r(z)) < infinity (integrableOn_mult), H integrable on B_r(z), mu-a.e. point in spt V, and the projection facts ||A|| <= |A|, |p_{T^perp} v| = infDist(v, T), trace(p_{T^perp} p_P) = |p_P - p_T|^2/2, |p_P - p_T|^2 <= 4n
Cutoff zeta(x) = phi(|x - z|/r) with phi a C^infinity 3-Lipschitz step (1 on (-inf, 1/2], 0 on [1, inf)): zeta = 1 on B_{r/2}(z), zeta = 0 off B^o_r(z), ||D zeta|| <= 3/r
Test field X = zeta^2 p_{T^perp}(x - z) is C^infinity with tsupport in B_r(z) contained in U; mu-a.e. div_M X = zeta^2 s + 2 zeta D zeta((p_x - p_T) x'), s = |p_x - p_T|^2/2
All integrands are mu-integrable; the first-variation identity gives integral zeta^2 s = - integral 2 zeta D zeta((p_x - p_T) x') - integral zeta^2 <x', H>
Young absorption: integral zeta^2 s <= 8 integral ||D zeta||^2 |x'|^2 + 2 integral zeta^2 |x'| |H|
zeta = 1 on B_{r/2}(z), ||D zeta|| <= 3/r, |x'| <= h mu-a.e. on B_r(z) give the constants 144 and 4
